content.title: About
content.content: Rutabaga, also known as swede or yellow turnip, is a root vegetable from the Brassicaceae family. Raw rutabaga has a firm, slightly sweet flesh, a crisp texture and a mildly bitter undertone. It is often used in salads, quick pickles, or as a crunchy addition to fresh dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rutabaga is a hybrid of cabbage and turnip that originated in Scandinavia.
Unlike many root vegetables, it can be stored in a cool place for up to six months.
It contains higher levels of glucosinolates than most Brassica vegetables, giving it a distinctive aroma.
In Japan, thinly sliced raw rutabaga is used in a traditional dish called "tsunaka" where it is pickled in vinegar.
The leafy tops are edible and rich in vitamins.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Rutabaga provides a good amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Its fiber content promotes healthy digestion and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium aids in electrolyte balance and normal heart function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Raw rutabaga has a low energy density, making it a suitable choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: High in glucosinolates
items.content: These compounds may support detoxification processes and offer protection against certain cancers.

items.title: Allergy to cruciferous vegetables
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to members of the Brassicaceae family, including rutabaga.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Rutabaga contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: May cause digestive discomfort in large amounts
items.content: The high fiber level can lead to gas and bloating if consumed excessively.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice raw rutabaga thinly for salads, add it to fresh vegetable mixes, quick‑pickle it in vinegar, or use it as a crunchy garnish for fish and meat dishes. Be sure to wash it thoroughly before eating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store rutabaga in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or a container with a damp cloth. Properly stored, it stays fresh for 2–3 weeks. Remove any damaged roots to prevent spoilage of the rest.
